fun_fact: The Aravallis are the oldest mountain range in India — and one of the hardest-working. They recharge groundwater, shelter wildlife, and act as a green wall that keeps the Thar desert from swallowing the Indo-Gangetic plain, which would be a desert without them. Yet they're under threat: unrestrained mining is eating into the range, and a new ruling that only hills above 100 metres qualify for protection puts the range at even greater risk.
